reader.requirement: At --std 85, when the merge file (file-name-1) has only fixed length records, each record of a USING file (file-name-2 or file-name-3) shorter than that fixed length must be released space filled on the right from the position after its last character, whatever the USING file's organization and whether it is fixed or variable; the fixed length is integer-1 of a format 1 RECORD clause or, with no clause, the record description's size.
reader.edition-search: grep for DialectLevel, CobolVersion, DialectBehavior, IsActive, Constructs in SortEmitter.cs (EmitInputFile, EmitGivingFile), CobolSort.cs (FillTo, Release), RecordFill.cs and FileModel.cs (ShortRecordFillNational, RecordSizeVaries, RecordWidth): none consults the edition; the fill is one code path for every edition. The only edition-dependent input is whether the file is fixed length, decided by the RECORD clause binding (format 3 is variable at every edition, docs/conformance DOC-A.1-148).
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf33_02 covers variable-length sequential USING files into a fixed SD of RECORD CONTAINS 6; not exercised are fixed USING files shorter than the SD, relative and indexed USING files, a USING file with two record sizes and no RECORD clause, an SD with no RECORD clause, and an SD whose RECORD CONTAINS exceeds its record description.

probes.expected: fixed sequential (2), relative (3), indexed (4) and two-size sequential (2/5) USING records released to a fixed 6-character SD (no RECORD clause, a numeric last item) space filled to 6; the area preset to X shows no X

reader.notes: EmitInputFile releases a fixed SD's records through CobolSort.FillTo(image, sdFile.RecordWidth, ...), and RecordWidth is max(integer-1, the largest record description), so a short USING record of any organization is space filled to the SD's fixed length; a variable SD takes the record at its read size instead (GR7b). Probed at --std 85 for sequential, relative and indexed USING files: all filled as the rule says.

refuter.evidence: q4a at --std 85: USING a VARYING 1..3 sequential file (records of 1 and 3) and a DYNAMIC indexed file of 2-char records; MERGE into SD SM RECORD CONTAINS 8 over a 3-char 01 plus an 8-char 01 preset to # before each RETURN: M-[A       ] M-[B2      ] M-[C33     ] M-[D2      ] (filled to integer-1 = 8); MERGE into SD SN with no RECORD clause, 01s of 3 and 6: N-[A     ] N-[B2    ] N-[C33   ] N-[D2    ] (filled to the implementor's fixed 6). cite.py: OK §1985:XI.4.1.4 GR2; OK §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR3.
